summary: 2 RED violations detected (explicit nationality/language targeting: 'bilingual residents,' 'perfect for Hispanic families'). 2 YELLOW cautions (ethnic market as neighborhood marker). CRITICAL: explicit discrimination based on national origin and language. Immediate rewrite required before publication.

red_violations.original_text: Walking distance to Spanish-language schools and ethnic market
red_violations.violation_type: National Origin and Language Discrimination (Explicit Targeting)
red_violations.authority: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. §3604(b) (National origin); 24 CFR §100.75
red_violations.risk_level: CRITICAL — Direct violation; explicit discrimination by national origin and language
red_violations.legal_basis: Targeting 'Spanish-language schools' and 'ethnic market' explicitly limits the property's marketed appeal to Spanish-speaking residents, excluding English-speaking and other-language-speaking households. This is direct discrimination based on national origin and language — prohibited bases under Fair Housing Act.
red_violations.suggested_rewrite: Walking distance to schools and neighborhood retail shopping
red_violations.citation: Fair Housing Act §3604(b); 24 CFR §100.75; HUD Guidance on national origin and language discrimination

red_violations.authority: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. §3604(b) (National origin); 24 CFR §100.75
red_violations.risk_level: CRITICAL — Direct violation; explicit targeting of protected national-origin class
red_violations.legal_basis: Explicitly marketing property to 'Hispanic families' targets a national-origin group and implicitly excludes other national-origin groups. Fair Housing Act protects national origin as a class. Any listing copy that targets or excludes based on national origin, ethnicity, or language is a direct violation.
red_violations.suggested_rewrite: Spacious home ideal for households of all sizes
red_violations.citation: Fair Housing Act §3604(b); 24 CFR §100.75 — National origin as prohibited basis

yellow_cautions.original_text: Vibrant, international community with bilingual residents
yellow_cautions.caution_type: Possible National Origin Coding (When Used as Sole Descriptor)
yellow_cautions.authority: HUD Fair Housing Guidance (2016); Fair Housing case law on neighborhood descriptors
yellow_cautions.risk_level: MEDIUM — Contextual; becomes RED when paired with 'Spanish-language' and 'Hispanic' language above
yellow_cautions.legal_basis: 'International community' and 'bilingual residents' document that non-English speakers are present. Standing alone, this might be a factual neighborhood descriptor. However, paired with 'Spanish-language schools' and 'perfect for Hispanic families,' it becomes part of an explicit national-origin targeting narrative.
yellow_cautions.suggested_rewrite: [Omit if used solely to target non-English speakers] or 'Diverse neighborhood with multiple cultural communities'
yellow_cautions.note: Becomes RED in context of explicit Hispanic targeting. The violation is the targeting, not the descriptor itself.
yellow_cautions.citation: HUD Fair Housing Guidance (2016); Fair Housing case law on neighborhood markers

yellow_cautions.original_text: Authentic cultural atmosphere with traditional restaurants nearby
yellow_cautions.caution_type: Ethnic Descriptor (When Used as Sole Neighborhood Marker)
yellow_cautions.authority: HUD Fair Housing Guidance (2016); Fair Housing Council case law
yellow_cautions.risk_level: MEDIUM — Contextual; compounds national-origin targeting above
yellow_cautions.legal_basis: 'Authentic cultural atmosphere' and 'traditional restaurants' are ethnic descriptors. HUD guidance notes that such descriptors can signal exclusion when used as the *only* way to market a neighborhood or when paired with national-origin targeting. Here, paired with explicit 'Hispanic families' language, they reinforce national-origin discrimination.
yellow_cautions.suggested_rewrite: [Omit or replace with neutral amenity language] 'Fine dining and cultural events nearby' or specific restaurant/venue names
yellow_cautions.note: Factual amenity only if truly central to property appeal. When used to code for specific ethnic/national-origin groups, it becomes part of discrimination pattern.
yellow_cautions.citation: HUD Fair Housing Guidance (2016); Fair Housing Council v. 1734 East 82nd Street (9th Cir. 2019)

before_after_sample.original_excerpt: Vibrant, international community with bilingual residents. Walking distance to Spanish-language schools and ethnic market. Perfect for Hispanic families. Authentic cultural atmosphere with traditional restaurants nearby.
before_after_sample.compliant_version: Vibrant neighborhood with diverse dining and cultural events. Walking distance to schools and retail shopping. Spacious home ideal for households of all sizes. Multiple restaurants and entertainment venues nearby. Move-in ready.

defensibility_statement: This listing has been audited against HUD 24 CFR §100.75 (Fair Housing Act prohibited bases in advertising) and Fair Housing Act §3604(b) (National origin discrimination). Two CRITICAL RED violations are documented below. This listing carries severe liability risk and requires immediate rewrite before publication. Compliant version eliminates all national-origin targeting while preserving neighborhood appeal. This audit creates a defensible record showing good-faith compliance effort.

agent_education.headline: National origin and language targeting is a CRITICAL Fair Housing Act violation — and sometimes goes undetected in multi-cultural markets.
agent_education.pattern: This listing uses four phrases that explicitly target Hispanic/Spanish-speaking residents: 'bilingual residents,' 'Spanish-language schools,' 'perfect for Hispanic families,' and 'authentic cultural atmosphere.' While diversity is an asset, using it to exclude other national-origin groups violates Fair Housing law. The listing does not say 'not for English speakers,' but it clearly markets to one national-origin group, implicitly excluding others.
agent_education.fix_approach: Remove all national-origin and language references. Replace 'Spanish-language schools' with factual 'schools'; remove 'perfect for Hispanic families' entirely; replace 'bilingual residents' with 'diverse community'; omit 'authentic cultural atmosphere' or replace with 'fine dining.' The neighborhood's actual appeal (diverse dining, cultural events, walkable schools) remains; the exclusionary national-origin framing is removed.
agent_education.compliance_benefit: National origin discrimination is a CRITICAL violation trigger. HUD actively enforces this category with severe penalties ($16K–$55K+ per violation, plus attorney fees). Compliant listings avoid this reputational and legal catastrophe. Marketing to 'all buyers' (not targeted national-origin groups) expands market reach and protects the agent.
